A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DreamPartGen and PartRel3D. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite extensive reformatting and some reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, component and conditioning ablations, robustness evaluations, scene-generation results, and a dataset annotation audit.

after.justification: v2 retains original DreamPartGen experimental results in the main text and appendices, including generation, ablation, robustness, and dataset-validation outcomes.

M1.justification: The DPL/RSL architecture, synchronization updates, diffusion objectives, inference procedure, and application procedures remain unchanged. Newly specifying that fusion coefficients are learnable documents an existing component without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both retain Objaverse, ShapeNet, ABO and PartRel3D generation, PartVerse alignment, PartVerse/PartNet VAE fine-tuning, and 3D-Front scene evaluation including occlusion. Rare-part and held-out-relation scenarios also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained within corresponding experiments: Trellis, CLAY, HoloPart and PartCrafter for object/alignment comparisons; HoloPart and PartCrafter for part and robustness comparisons; MIDI and PartCrafter for scenes. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported conditioning evaluation drops the Text+Image control from v1 Table 5 to v2 Table 6. Other documented settings remain stable, including training hyperparameters, voxelization resolution and F-score threshold. Table 3's new 'fixed random subset' description is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed split or rerun.

E4.justification: Removing the Text+Image ablation reduces evidence isolating the benefit of relational inputs when text and image are already supplied. Component, token-count, parser, rare-part and held-out-relation analyses otherwise remain; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Both describe 20 annotation-audit repetitions with 200 triplets per repetition. Neither introduces generation-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 and the conditioning table exchange CD/EMD assignments; for example, Table 3's full-model pair changes from 0.771/0.145 to 0.145/0.771. The Text+Image row disappears, and headline reductions change from 53%/33% to 60%/41% despite unchanged Table 1 scores. Appendix KID entries become uniformly 1,000 times larger without a stated scale conversion. These are reporting revisions, not demonstrated performance gains; most results and rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–6 retain the same substance. Explicitly describing global tokens as non-diffusion variables clarifies the previously documented deterministic update; no theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The claimed average geometric improvements increase from 53% CD and 33% EMD to 60% and 41% in the abstract/introduction and results summary. The central DPL/RSL contribution, PartRel3D contribution and application scope remain the same.

C2.justification: Appendix C corrects the claim that spatial triplets alone perform best: v2 identifies text as strongest overall among single inputs and locates the spatial-triplet benefit in Text+ST. The full-input caption narrows 'all metrics' to 'most metrics.' The conclusion replaces general embodied-interaction directions with extending the method to densely entangled structures such as bushes.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies learnable fusion coefficients in Section 3.3 and a fixed random PartRel3D subset in Table 3. These improve documentation without establishing implementation or experimental changes. Optimizer settings, GPU hardware and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds AutoPartGen, FullPart, PARIS3D and PartSLIP, while removing five earlier citations, including DreamBooth3D and PALM. It more explicitly distinguishes vision-language-based part perception from generation. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained with localized clarification and correction. Qualitative and quantitative ablation discussions are reordered, dataset and implementation appendices exchange order, inference efficiency moves into the main text, and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column design to a single-column format, with pervasive changes to typography, headings, figure/table sizing and placement, and text wrapping around displays. Appendix timing Table 10 becomes main-text Table 4. Existing illustrations are retained with caption and label edits.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the unsupported ST-alone superiority interpretation and replaces the 53%/33% headline with 60%/41%, consistent with approximately 59.8%/40.7% mean reductions calculated from unchanged Table 1. These repairs modestly improve accuracy. The benefit is limited by unexplained KID rescaling and removal of the useful Text+Image control; there is no substantive expansion of empirical evidence.
